article.title: Topic chains and referent tracking in Chinese discourse
article.chapter: Norma, estilo y elección avanzada C2 — 規範、文體與進階選擇 C2

claims.summary: Li examines Chinese topic chains in written narrative, where zero noun phrases are understood through their referential relations in discourse.
In six chapters of Luotuo Xiangzi, Li found 81 sentence/chain-initial zero NPs: 75 cataphoric and 6 anaphoric; the study reports that chain topics need not always be overtly mentioned first.

Yang et al.'s experiments found no significant reaction-time difference between topic-continuous and topic-discontinuous conditions for zero-anaphora resolution in the reported experiment and also reported a first-mention effect under specified conditions.

Checking the possible antecedent of a zero NP before adding a connector or repeating a name is an editorial inference from the studies' evidence that reference can be anaphoric or cataphoric and context-sensitive; it is not a universal grammatical prescription.

Li's evidence is from six chapters of one Chinese novel and Yang et al.'s evidence is experimental; these sources do not validate the entry's removed education/market examples or establish universal academic, conversational, or Taiwan-Mandarin rules.

links.notes: Li states the study examines topic-chain structure and written narrative and explains that Chinese discourse uses zero NPs whose interpretation is linked to topic chains.
Reports the six chapters, 81 cases, 75 cataphoric and six anaphoric zero NPs, and explains that topics need not always appear overtly in the first link.
The authors report no significant RT difference for topic continuity/discontinuity in Experiment 1a and a first-mention effect in the specified voice/situation conditions in Experiment 5.
The study demonstrates anaphoric and cataphoric zero-NP links and discusses how comprehenders use contextual information; the editing step is explicitly presented as an inference from these findings.
The experiment cautions against a simple one-direction claim that topic continuity always yields faster resolution.
Li specifies that the quantitative sample covers six chapters of Luotuo Xiangzi and describes those data rather than all genres or dialects.
Yang et al. report experiment-specific materials and findings; they do not establish an unrestricted writing rule.
